immunology.way_of_thinking: The art of keeping life alive. Find the fault that is actually present, reproduce it with a failing test, fix exactly that and nothing around it. A fix larger than its fault is an overshoot, the same harm as the fault, so refuse the tidy-up, the extra option and the new abstraction. Confirm the patient is still well afterwards: the test turns green and reverting the fix turns it red again.

oncology.way_of_thinking: The art of proportions: just enough, in the right place. Be careful before being clever. Measure the size of the problem first, then use the smallest amount of Rust that closes it, with types that make the wrong state impossible and an error for every missing case. Anything that grows without a reason (code, unsafe, speed work, dependencies) is the thing to cut.
